# **Purpose** {#purpose}

The purpose of this working group is to provide maker organizations information and coordinate resources that aids those organizations in providing their membership a safe environment. 

# **How we are working on this?** {#how-we-are-working-on-this?}

In the short term the working group will focus our efforts on fire prevention strategies, but will expand those efforts to encompass electrical code, shop safety, and other areas that pertain to maker organizations.

1. Primary collaboration will be via the [Risk Management](https://nation-of-makers.slack.com/messages/risk_management/) channel on the Nation of Maker’s (NOM) Slack:  [https://nation-of-makers.slack.com/messages/risk\_management/](https://nation-of-makers.slack.com/messages/risk_management/).  
2. A conference call may be set-up, if needed:  
   1. Next Conference Call: Sunday, 1/8/2017 @ 8PM ET led by Robb Hendershot from Denhac.  More details in the [Risk Management](https://nation-of-makers.slack.com/messages/risk_management/details/) Slack channel.  
3. Anyone can contribute to this Working Document\!  
4. If interested in specific action items in the [Outreach](#outreach:-how-can-nom-help?) let us know on Slack.  
5. When we release an item to our NOM community we will post it as PDF link into our NOMSafetyWorkingGroup Google account’s drive and provide a view only link to an Overview.  
   1. The short URL for this Overview is: [http://bit.ly/2jwzXhA](http://bit.ly/2jwzXhA)  
   2. Fermin Diaz has offered to provide released items in Spanish.  
      1. [ferminjdiaz@hotmail.com](mailto:ferminjdiaz@hotmail.com)

# **Impacted Areas from Ghost Ship Fire** {#impacted-areas-from-ghost-ship-fire}

**NOTE:** All of the instances below that we’ve seen thus far are within Artist Spaces used either as Living Spaces or Performance Spaces.  **There has been heightened awareness to authorities to take action for these Artist Spaces.** Two main causes for closures were:

* **Change of Use:**  The landlord was not aware or was not willing to enforce before the Ghost Ship fire: Living arrangements that were going on or large Events in the spaces.  These activities were not within their lease contract.  
* **Fire & Safety Infractions:** Violations in Fire & Safety Codes. 

**Stages:** Incident, Evictions, Event warnings, Concerns

# **Outreach: How Can NOM Help?** {#outreach:-how-can-nom-help?}

Based on a local meeting in Oakland[^1] hosted by Omni Commons after the Ghost Ship tragedy a recommended set of action items was identified by those in attendance to help in the Bay Area, this Safety working group put together the following diagram to help with communicating a context for what we are wanting to accomplish and to focus efforts on immediate versus long-term activities:

![][image1]

The Safety Working Group has identified five key stages of the lifecycle of spaces and their needs for safety assistance[^2]:

1. ***Pre-Construction Education**:* *“What sort of space should I rent/buy?”*  
2. ***Pre-Opening:** “Do we have all our safety fundamentals complete?”*  
3. ***In Operation:**  “When was the last Safety Check? Who performed it?”*  
4. ***Immediate Needs:*** “*Oh, no\! The Fire Marshal is coming. Let’s re-check things.“*  
5. ***Long-Term:*** “*I want to change how I’m using my space.*” 

*For the next month (target end date of 1/12/2017) the Safety Working Group will focus on any Advocacy, Aid Networks, Fundraising and Information recommendations for spaces in the **Immediate Need** stage.*  Assumptions as we targeted our communication and focus on what to recommend/ask in the table below:

* CAN NOT HELP: We can't really help people using a space in an illegal way, and are getting kicked out by the landlord because of it.  
* CAN HELP A LITTLE: Someone using a space in an illegal way, who wants to get legal, and got a violation from the City. Might be too hard and take a lot more time to help since it may take changes to zoning and / or it is tied to their lease.  
* CAN HELP THE MOST:  Someone using the space they have in a legal way, and need help doing so.  For example, they have a commercial space, using for Making, don't live in it, but had no idea that they had to follow certain fire codes and now are in trouble.

***For this next month (target end date of 1/12/2017) the Safety Working Group will focus on helping spaces with Immediate Needs as follows:***

| Safety Assistance | Working Group Actions \[*Highlighted in Orange in the Overview diagram above*\] |
| :---- | ----- |
| *Advocacy* | Provide one-pager for How To Interface with the various authorities for spaces (e.g. Here's ***How to Talk to the Fire Marshal***) Provide one-pager targeted to Authorities (for now, Property Owners and Fire Marshals) advocating and indicating what makerspaces are. |
| *Aid Networks* | Ask if makerspaces are willing and able to reach out to DIY spaces close to them to see if they need help. Redirect back to Working Group as needed. When requested, we can connect and coordinate smaller local groups When requested, we can steer people to the correct local groups |
| *Funding* | At this time, NOM can not receive donations and is not prepared to distribute any funds.   Provide a one-pager with list of potential outside funding resources that spaces can pursue on their own. |
| *Information* | Provide a one-pager Fire Safety Fundamentals with suggestions targeted for primary “space owner” membership |

We will leverage the NOM communication channels available via email through:

* Current email subscribers to the Nation Of Makers website ([http://nationofmakers.us](http://nationofmakers.us) )  
* Current Makerspace network collected by state representatives that attended the White House session in June 2016\.  
* Current Nation of Makers \- Makerspace Organizers Facebook group  
* Current Nation of Makers \- State Ambassadors Facebook group

# **Reference Guide** {#reference-guide}

After a quick perusal of the original Problem Statements I found the following related to Risk Management in the area of safety and training:

1. It is difficult for each space to create material for the training and tracking of member safety instruction or certifications.  
2. Members of a space require clear, consistent training and documentation on key areas such as safety training, operational guides/best practices for key equipment.  
3. Spaces often face challenge to figure out what laws, ordinances, zoning rules, or other guidelines apply to them.  
4. Housekeeping is an ongoing challenge for spaces as members’ projects are often not cleaned up while in process or at the completion, occupying space and tools that others could be using.  
5. Many Makerspaces have limited resources or knowledge to dispose of wastes such as e-waste, hazardous chemicals, or biological, or other non-standard waste.

## **Topics** {#topics}

Waste Disposal

* 

Upkeep/Maintenance

* Safety Checks (What, When/Frequency)

Safety Orientations

* Space Orientation \[Evacuations\]  
* Equipment Orientations  
* Processes for Tracking Who Has Been Trained

Education and Training

* How to find applicable laws/rules/guidelines.

# **APPENDIX III:  Discussion on “The Codes”** {#appendix-iii:- discussion-on-“the-codes”}

Capture of the highlights of a discussion in Slack on December 12th, 2016 with Jeffrey McGrew on the different codes:

* National, Industry or International Code Standards come out every three years.  
* Building Code, Fire Code, Electrical Code, and those sorts of 'how it gets built' codes are all based upon International Codes.  
* These International Code Standards get adopted into the State Code, which then gets additional modifications from the county or city to be the ‘local code’.  
* Another complexity is Zoning / Planning Code.  
* “How It’s Built” can be generalized, but “What Can Go Where” can’t be generalized.

# **APPENDIX IV:  Email Draft for 12/16/2016** {#appendix-iv:- email-draft-for-12/16/2016}

The following is an email template that we are targeting to send out by Friday, 12/13/2016 through the following existing NOM communication channels:

* Current email subscribers to the Nation Of Makers website ([http://nationofmakers.org](http://nationofmakers.org) )  
* Current Makerspace network collected by state representatives that attended the White House session in June 2016\.  
* Current Nation of Makers \- Makerspace Organizers Facebook group  
* Current Nation of Makers \- State Ambassadors Facebook group

**\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*  NOTE:  THIS IS NOT THE OFFICIAL VERSION THAT WENT OUT  \*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\***  
\------------- BEGINS HERE------------

In response to the recent Ghost Ship tragedy in Oakland and news of crackdowns on DIY spaces across the country, a group of individuals within the Nation of Makers [\#Risk \_Management](https://nation-of-makers.slack.com/messages/risk_management/) Slack channel initiated a Safety Working Group to address any outreach needed in the NoM community.  This Working Group has set out to provide maker and artist organizers support through information and coordination that aid in providing their community and environment that meets local fire and safety code. 

![][image2]

The Safety Working Group has identified three key stages of the lifecycle of spaces and their needs for safety assistance:

1. **Pre-construction Education** *“What sort of space should I rent/buy?”*  
2. **Immediate Needs** *“Oh no, the fire marshal is coming\!”*  
3. **Long-Term** *“Let's turn this DIY space legal.”*

Due to the concerns and urgency to protect existing spaces that are at risk due to the Ghost Ship fire, the Safety Working Group will focus on the following deliverables over the next month (shown in orange in the diagram above):

* Quick reference guide ***for space leaders*** on how to interface with various authorities  
* Quick reference guide ***for authorities and property*** ***owners*** advocating and indicating what makerspaces are  
* List of potential outside **funding resources** since NOM is unable to collect or distribute donations as a 5013c at this time.  
* Quick reference guide on ***Fire Safety Fundamentals***

In the spirit of lending a hand, if you know of maker or artist spaces in your community that could be struggling with safety hazards or code violations, we encourage you to reach out to them to relay this information and offer what help you can.  Through our collective insight, pooled resources, and the sheer expanse of our network-the community built here within NOM has the immense capacity to help spaces in need\! 

As we finish with these ***Immediate Needs*** to help spaces, we invite others to join us in providing safety assistance to address ***Pre-Construction*** and ***Long-Term*** needs.  For anyone looking to get involved, provide feedback, or ask questions, please reach out to us\!

The Safety Working Group  
[\#Risk\_Management](https://nation-of-makers.slack.com/messages/risk_management/) Slack Channel  
[NOMSafetyWorkingGroup@gmail.com](mailto:NOMSafetyWorkingGroup@gmail.com)  
For more information on items available thus far go to: [http://bit.ly/2gD3Tag](http://bit.ly/2gD3Tag)
